data.narrative:
Deep Fission, a nuclear energy company founded by Liz Muller and Rich Muller, is preparing for IPO following $80M in total capital raised. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 8 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (X-Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy), all operating in the nuclear energy sector.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. The nuclear energy sector contains only 5 same-sector peers overall, with none meeting the threshold of 3 or more datapoints when filtered by stage-matching or valuation-tier similarity. A same-stage peer count of 1, adjacent-stage count of 0, and similar-tier count of 0 preclude robust median triangulation. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce material distortion given Deep Fission's specialized technology positioning.

Without sufficient narrow-stage comps to establish a peer-median baseline, this analysis cannot produce a supported valuation range at this time. Key uncertainties limiting the valuation include the absence of direct IPO-stage precedents in advanced nuclear, limited public market comparability data, and the nascent maturity of the frontier nuclear subsector. A defensible range would require either (1) expansion of the peer set to adjacent technologies or stages, or (2) primary market data on recent nuclear technology financings at comparable scale.
